title: KPI Prioritizer: Roadmap Accordion & Go-Live Blueprint
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for the 'Roadmap Accordion' — a compact way to prioritize features by KPI impact, risk, and runway effort — and the companion 'Decision Arc' triggers that map KPI breaches to concrete go/no-go actions during rollouts. Use this as the canonical working doc for next three quarters of activation planning and to feed the launch checklist template.

Summary (one-liner):
Create a small-surface, high-value roadmap ordering mechanism (Accordion) that folds/unfolds by KPI sensitivity and pairs with an escalation Decision Arc so product ops, SRE, and eng can make consistent rollout calls under traffic stress.

How to use this doc:
- OWNER maintains the accordion entries and threshold numbers.
- Weekly product-ops sync: review changed KPIs, move items up/down accordion.
- Incident mode: follow Decision Arc -> triage plays -> apply traffic triage.

Roadmap Accordion structure (rows are accordion panels; each panel folded in weekly view):
1) Panel: "Latency-first UX"
   - Hypothesis: 95th P95 token latency reduction -> improves trial-to-paid conversion by 3–5% for interactive features.
   - Primary KPI: P95 latency (ms) end-to-end (API -> model).
   - Secondary KPIs: error-rate, median latency, cost per 1k tokens.
   - Estimated dev effort: 4 sprint-weeks (cross-eng + infra)
   - Impact score (1–10): 8
   - Owners: Product: Priya Rao; Eng: Diego Alvarez; SRE: Marcus Holloway
   - Notes: canary rollout required; fallback to smaller model variant under heavy load.

2) Panel: "Embed Cache & Routing"
   - Hypothesis: intelligent routing + local embedding cache reduces embedding unit costs by ~30% for search-heavy customers.
   - Primary KPI: embedding-unit cost ($/1M queries) and cache hit rate (%)
   - Dev effort: 3 sprint-weeks + infra config
   - Impact score: 7
   - Owners: Product: Avery Chen; Eng: Nina Patel
   - Notes: requires Dedicated capacity gating for early customers.

3) Panel: "Batching Presets & Adaptive Window"
   - Hypothesis: workload-aware batching improves throughput without hurting 95th percentile latency for short queries.
   - KPIs: tokens/sec per GPU, P95 latency on small queries, cost per token
   - Dev effort: 5 sprint-weeks (runtime + platform)
   - Impact score: 9
   - Owners: Eng-runtime: K. Sugimoto; Platform: Diego Alvarez

4) Panel: "Rollout Instrumentation & Guardrails"
   - Hypothesis: better telemetry and automatic guardrails reduce mean time to rollback and false-positive degradations.
   - KPIs: time-to-detect (minutes), mean-time-to-rollback, number of false alarms/week
   - Dev effort: 2 sprint-weeks
   - Impact score: 6
   - Owners: Product-ops: Avery Chen; Observability: Hannah Price

Decision Arc: mapping KPI breaches to actions (compact, numbered arc):
- Arc 0 (Green): All KPIs within thresholds -> normal rollout.
- Arc 1 (Amber): Any secondary KPI breached (e.g., error-rate > 1% OR P50 latency +30% over baseline) -> throttle new traffic by 25%, increase sampling & tracing, notify oncall and product ops.
- Arc 2 (Red): Primary KPI breach (e.g., P95 latency > 2x baseline OR 5xx spikes) -> immediate rollback to previous model variant, enable degraded mode (non-streaming), escalate to SRE and Product-ops commander.
- Arc 3 (Critical): Sustained regional outage or data-leak suspicion -> full traffic cutover to cold fallback and exec notification.

Threshold examples (set during preflight; these are starting numbers to tune):
- P95 latency: baseline 350ms -> Amber at 525ms (+50%), Red at 700ms (+100%)
- Error-rate (5xx): Amber at 1%, Red at 3%
- Embedding cost per 1M: Amber at +20% vs baseline, Red at +50%

Traffic Triage Playbook (fast checklist for oncall and product ops):
1) Confirm metric source and sampling window (90s)
2) Reproduce locally with a low-volume probe to rule out telemetry noise
3) If Arc1: invoke 'soft throttle' - reduce new session acceptance by 25% for 10 minutes -> observe
4) If Arc2: trigger rollback play, move traffic to model-variant vX-1, cut streaming if needed
5) If Arc3: follow SEV-1 runbook (link below) and notify GTM and CSM for customer comms

Preflight Go-Live Checklist (must pass all items; owners sign off):
- [ ] KPI Baseline captured (48h of representative traffic) -> Owner: Observability
- [ ] Canary plan documented (traffic %, duration, sampling windows) -> Owner: Product-ops
- [ ] Escalation contacts verified and on-call roster updated -> Owner: SRE
- [ ] Fallback model variant validated and warm -> Owner: Serving-runtime
- [ ] Cost guardrails configured (budget alerts, rate limits) -> Owner: Finance & Platform
- [ ] Customer comms draft ready for first 24h incidents -> Owner: CS
- [ ] Privacy & compliance checklist signed (if private deploy) -> Owner: Security

KPI sheet (quick reference lines for each top-priority panel):
- Latency-first UX: P95, median, 5xx (baseline: 350ms / 120ms / 0.4%)
- Embed Cache: cache-hit %, cost/1M (baseline: 12% / $540)
- Batching Presets: tokens/sec/GPU, P95-short (baseline: 45k t/s / 380ms)
- Instrumentation: time-to-detect, mttr (baseline: 8m / 22m)

Operational notes & heuristics (less formal):
- Small tweaks that reduce P95 by 40–60ms: lower max prefix length for interactive tier, reduce default temperature for short prompts, and bump kv-cache prefetch parallelism (runtime change).
- If embedding cost spikes after a release, look first at routing table changes and caching TTLs — most regressions are config-related.
- For Dedicated customers with strict SLAs, pre-authorize fallback model families; avoid auto-quantization switches during first 7 days after rollout.

Meeting cadence & artifacts to keep updated:
- Weekly Roadmap Accordion review (product-ops): update impact scores and move panels as data arrives.
- Canary preflight mini-retro within 24h of completion.
- Post-mortem within 5 business days after any Arc2/Arc3 event.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add experiment to quantify conversion lift from 40ms P95 improvement (A/B design needed). -> OWNER: Priya
- Work with finance to simulate cost thresholds for 3 dedicated customers with heavy embedding volume. -> OWNER: Avery
- Draft customer-facing incident template for embed-cost spikes. -> OWNER: Nina

References & quick links:
- SEV runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/SEV-Runbook
- Canary checklist template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Canary-Checklist
- Relevant PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/812
- Jira: JIRA-3456 (Accordion UI for Console)

If you edit this doc: prefix edits with initials + date, keep the accordion panels numbered, and avoid removing threshold history (we need delta history for postmortems).

Last note: This is intentionally concise — the accordion is meant to be a low-friction decision aid. If we try to capture every metric we will lose speed. Keep to 3–6 panels at a time and rotate the lower-impact items out each quarter.

Signed-off-by: Avery Chen (product-ops)
